description: Japan national university standard tuition fee (授業料標準額) and admission fee (入学料標準額), annual, in Japanese Yen. Set by Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology (MEXT). From 2004, national universities became independent corporations; the government sets a "standard amount" (標準額) and individual universities may charge up to 20% above it. The 535,800 yen standard has been unchanged since 2005. Before 1975, national university education was free or near-free.
source: Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Japan (文部科学省)
note: Pre-2004: fees set directly by government ordinance, uniform across all national universities. Post-2004: national university corporations may set their own fees up to 20% above the standard. In practice, almost all national universities charge exactly the standard amount. Separate admission fee (入学料) also applies on entry: 282,000 yen standard since 2005. Private university fees are substantially higher and vary by institution.
keyFacts: Free (no tuition) 1947-1974 under post-war education system
Fees increased almost every year 1975-2004 as government gradually reduced subsidies
National University Corporation reform 2004: universities became independent; government sets standard amount
Standard amount frozen at 535,800 yen since 2005 (21 consecutive years unchanged as of 2025)
Private universities charge an average of approx 900,000-1,300,000 yen/year (much higher)
Free tuition for low-income students introduced 2020 under High School/University Education Free Act
